strategy.summary: Owner-led family foundry (since 1921) supplying two grey-iron volute casings. On part:310010 it is our sole active source (100% quota). It is priced at or slightly below its own should-cost after four years of 'accepted below full cost to keep the volume'. It now asks +9.5% from 1 Nov, on notice that breaches clause 3.1. The checkable drivers support only about +2.3%, and its costing is admittedly stale. On part:310012 it holds 40% quota and sits about 10% above its own should-cost and above the co-source Wimbacher, so there is real room downward there. It wants cash: it asked for 10-day payment against a discount. It also wants volume and recognition of past partnership. Delivery (class B amber) and quality on part:310010 are weak. Best route: grant a modest, index-justified increase on part:310010 from the new calendar year, paid for with faster payment, binding growth volume and a 24-month term. Offset it with a decrease on part:310012. Keep the tone warm and respectful of the owner.
strategy.decision_maker: The owner personally (visits, calls, price talks); costing is prepared by his office manager.

persona.owner_type: family-owned GmbH & Co. KG, owner-managed, mid-sized foundry
persona.style: Personal, relationship- and reciprocity-driven. Formal and apologetic in writing; invokes past favours. Not numbers-driven: works from an outdated spreadsheet.
other_traits: Owner admitted not tracking material/energy prices since the 2022 peak
Historically settles about 2-3 pp below its ask
Overpriced on part:310012 versus co-source, likely cross-subsidising part:310010

needs.detail: Asked for 10-day payment and offers a cash discount in return. We currently pay slightly late on most invoices.
Owner twice reminded us of the 2022 quarter at the old price and expects partnership in return.
Margin recovery on part:310010, which sits around or below full cost after repeated cuts.
Has repeatedly traded price for keeping volume. The growth forecasts for both parts are shared with it.
A longer framework helps an owner-run foundry; the current contract expires and renews only year by year.

constraints.detail: Part:310010 price is below the bottom-up should-cost, though within the estimate's error band. There is no room to cut further.
The 9.5% ask rests on a spreadsheet two years old and not maintained since the 2022 peak.
Prices are fixed per calendar year with 90 days' notice. A mid-year November start is invalid; the earliest valid date is the new year. The renewal notice window closes very soon.
Part:310010 has no active second source. The qualified Polish source quoted dearer and slower.
Holiday shutdown: January call-offs must be placed before the break.

levers.why: Factual and contractual: moves any increase to the new calendar year without arguing about the amount.
Power is down over 12 months, which directly contradicts the energy claim in the letter. It also answers the owner's own question about index sources.
Honestly concedes the real labour rise. This builds credibility and frames the justified total as small.
Concedes the steel effect, completing the bridge to roughly +2% rather than +9.5%.
Growth volume is what this supplier has always valued; offer it as the trade for a smaller increase.
Its own-plant should-cost shows clear margin on part:310012, which supports a decrease there.
Higher volume and possibly a larger quota on part:310012 in exchange for a price cut.
The same part is bought cheaper from the co-source. Use it if it resists a part:310012 cut; it reveals the rival's price.
Reminds it that it has historically settled well below its ask.
Recurring supplier-caused defects on the very part it wants to raise. Use as a fresh fact, factually and without blame.
On-time delivery is below the contract target. Use only as a late filler or if it claims reliability.
Ppm is above the peer median and an 8D is overdue. Use if it argues quality justifies a premium.
Shows the part can move to the co-source; use only if it stalls on part:310012.

trades.why: It asked for fast payment against a discount. Short payment is a cheap currency for us; offer it late in the round as the trade for a price step.
The contract already forbids the November start; anchor on the new calendar year.
24 months gives the owner security and partnership recognition; use it as an explicit trade for price.
Binding growth volume, within our forecast need, is what it has historically traded price for.
Weak quality on part:310010; add a tighter ppm target in return for accepting a modest increase.
No clause is asked for. Steel is rising, so a steel index clause would cost us; offer one only if it insists on long-term fixed prices.

price_view.reasoning: Part:310010 is at or below full cost and a below-cost price was accepted four times. The co-source quote is dearer, so a modest increase of about the index-justified level from the new year is fair and protects a needed supplier. The 9.5% ask is unsupported. Part:310012 has some room downward: it is about 10% above its own should-cost and above the co-source. Overall, a net small move bundling both parts is achievable.

do: Address the owner personally and acknowledge the long relationship and the 2022 gesture
Offer to share our index sources and figures as help, answering his own question
Concede the real cost drivers openly before showing the gap to the ask
Answer the payment request explicitly and constructively
Bundle both parts so the result feels like partnership, not a loss
dont: Do not imply the owner is incompetent or that his costing is stale; he admitted it in confidence
Do not threaten to move part:310010 to the Polish source
Do not ask open questions about his cost structure without bringing our own data
Do not cite copper, electronics or peak-based index falls
Do not demand long payment terms from a cash-seeking supplier

traps: Peak-based arguments (index_peak entries, power down since 2022) are not checkable and cost trust; use the 12-month changes instead
Rival quote for part:310010 (rival_quote:310010:8d1bfec0) is higher than its price and the ask; never cite it
should_cost:310010:9db147d7 and the price-trend and order-history 'for them' records support its case; do not cite them
Market news on copper, electronic boards and alloy 1.4404 is irrelevant to grey iron, and the steel/labour news helps them
Our late payment record invites a counter-complaint; do not raise payment discipline
Pushing part:310010 further below cost risks worse delivery and quality, or losing a sole source
The renewal notice deadline is close; decide on a deliberate exit or renewal, do not bluff an exit
strategy.writer_notes: Write to the owner by name, warmly and respectfully. Open by thanking him for the long partnership and the gesture he mentioned. Explain kindly that the contract fixes prices per calendar year, so any change applies from the new year. Share the official index figures he asked about: labour and steel up, power down. Show that together they support a small adjustment, not the asked one. Bring up quality and delivery only as facts and only later. Never use threats or deadlines, and always answer with a sheet.
questions_to_ask: Would a two-year agreement with binding volumes help your planning more than a higher price?
How much would faster payment be worth to you in the price?
Would it help if we shared the index series we use, so both sides calculate from the same figures?
Would you welcome a larger share of the bigger casing if the price there comes closer to the market?
What support would help you resolve the recurring marking and dimension defects on the smaller casing?

findings.text: Part 310010: price EUR 126.53 sits 4.6% BELOW our bottom-up should-cost of EUR 132.64 (no margin, ±5%). It has accepted below-cost prices on all 4 events since 2023. Price fell from 136.00 (2023) to 126.53 (-7.0%). There is no price room downward; a moderate increase is economically defensible, and for the supplier's health a below-cost price is a risk.

Part 310010 drivers justify roughly +2.3% over 12 months, not the 9.5% asked (EUR 138.55). Labour +2.7% (weight 0.32, about +0.85%), steel PPI-C241 +6.5% (weight 0.26, about +1.70%), power -3.7% (weight 0.06, about -0.22%). Copper and electronics news are irrelevant to grey-iron castings. Iron castings PPI is only +1.8% year on year.

Part 310010 rival benchmark: Kalwisz quoted EUR 143.22 (2026-09, 56d lead time, 60d payment), 13% above the current price and above the 138.55 ask. In 2025 Kalwisz quoted 124.20 against Brandlhuber's 142.50. The alternative now gives little price pressure; Brandlhuber is the cheapest source.

Part 310012: price EUR 383.06 is 10.3% ABOVE its own-plant should-cost (347.27). It is also 6.2% above Wimbacher's 359.17, both quoted (2026-09-05) and current order price, though Wimbacher wants 10-day payment. There is real room downward here: roughly 3-6% while still leaving a margin of about 4-7%. Drivers net about +2.2%, which only partly offsets this.

Cross-subsidy picture: across both parts its combined margin is close to zero-to-modest. A bundle trade (accept a small increase on 310010, a decrease on 310012) fits the economics. 310012 carries 40% quota and higher volume is forecast (2010 vs 1786).
Should-cost confidence is stated as 5% error; the 310010 below-cost finding (-4.6%) is within that error band, so treat it as 'around full cost' rather than certain loss.

Citing peak-based index falls is not checkable and costs trust
Revealing Wimbacher price on 310012 exposes rival data

findings.text: Owner-led family foundry (founded 1921, 185 staff, EUR 25.8M turnover). The owner personally handles the relationship: visits, calls and price talks. He thinks in terms of partnership and reciprocity and twice cited the 2022 quarter of supplying at the old price as a favour owed to us.

Its costing is stale. The owner works from a spreadsheet last updated two years ago and admitted he has not tracked material and energy prices since the 2022 peak; his office manager does the costing. The 9.5% ask (energy, raw material, wages) is therefore probably not based on current figures. Checkable indices give roughly +0.85% labour and +1.7% steel, while energy is down -0.22%: about +2.3% net, far below 9.5%. Handle this gently, since it is the owner's own admission.

It wants cash. It asked for payment within 10 days in exchange for a cash discount. We pay late on 84.1% of invoices (3.4 days on average, max 11) and have never taken a discount. Faster, punctual payment is a cheap currency for us to trade, and our late paying is a grievance they could raise.
The letter is formal and apologetic. Its notice of 51 days breaches the 90-day clause, and the clause fixes prices per calendar year, so a 2026-11-01 start cannot take effect as asked.

Its own price may sit below should-cost (EUR 126.53 vs 132.64 for part 310010). It has accepted below full cost to keep the volume on 4 events, and it cut prices 7% since 2023. Pressing too hard on a strategic casting risks margin stress and resentment.

Its finances are moderate and stable: equity ratio 24.7%, credit index 222 unchanged over 12 months, VDA 6.3 grade B. There are no signs of acute financial stress. We account for about 4.9% of its turnover.

The holiday shutdown runs 23 Dec to 6 Jan, and January call-offs are needed by 10 Dec, which is an operational sensitivity. No news exists about this supplier, so the evidence on its strategy is thin.

findings.text: Price is fixed per calendar year and any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end. The letter of 2026-09-11 asks +9.5% on part:310010 (EUR 126.53 to 138.55) from 2026-11-01. That is a mid-year change on 51 days' notice, so it cannot take effect as asked. The earliest possible date is 2027-01-01, and it was notified in time for that.

The framework agreement runs to 2026-12-31 and extends by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice. Notice to stop the renewal must be given by 2026-10-02. Until then we have a credible exit; after that both sides are bound into 2027. The exit is real for part:310012, which already has a second source. It is weak for part:310010, where the only alternative quoted dearer.

Other contract terms: payment 30 days net, against our standard of 60, which already benefits the supplier. Delivery is FCA with a 42-day lead time. The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint. The supplier misses the target at 85.2% on time and runs 712 ppm against a peer median of 457, with one 8D report overdue. The complaint fee is small: EUR 600 was recharged over 12 months.

Negotiation history: on both parts it has asked a little each year and settled about 2.4% below. Settlements were -5.6%, -0.1% and -1.4%, a gap of about 3 pp to its ask. Prices are down 7% since 2023. For part:310010 every event is recorded as 'accepted below full cost to keep the volume', and the should-cost model puts its price 4.6% below its own cost. This year's 9.5% ask is a sharp break from that pattern. It points to real margin pressure, but also to a costing spreadsheet the owner admits is two years out of date.

Dependency on part:310010: the supplier holds 100% quota and we own the tooling. The qualified PL source sup:70140 holds 0% quota and quoted EUR 143.22 with a 56-day lead time, above even the supplier's asked EUR 138.55. In practice we depend on this supplier for this part, so the tooling ownership is only a theoretical exit.

Dependency on part:310012: the supplier holds 40% quota, Wimbacher sup:70130 holds 60% and won the 2025 benchmark. Wimbacher is at EUR 359.17, against this supplier's EUR 383.06. The supplier is 10.3% above its own should-cost and we own the tooling, so our leverage on this part is strong.

Mutual dependence is moderate. Our spend is about EUR 1.26M, around 4.9% of its EUR 25.8M turnover, and has been growing. Forecast volumes are up about 10% on part:310010 and 12% on part:310012. The supplier is financially sound (credit index 222, stable) and could walk away. The owner repeatedly invokes the 2022 quarter in which they held the old price.

findings.text: Delivery is weak and has not improved. Rolling OTD against the requested date was 85.2% to 2026-09 (88.9% against its own confirmed date), down from 88.2% a year earlier, well below the 95% contract target and only level with the peer median of 84.6%. The scorecard has dropped from class A green to class B amber (score 84).

The delivery problem sits on part:310010. In the last 12 months only 78.6% of its receipts were on time against the requested date, 17.9% were late, late receipts averaged 14.8 days and the worst was 25 days. part:310012 ran at 92.3% on time with at most 10 days late. A recent PO was confirmed 9 days after the requested date.

Quality on part:310010 is a chronic problem. There were 15 QNs since 2024-06, 12 of them supplier-caused, and 6 complaints in the last 12 months. The rolling rate is 712 ppm against a peer median of 457 ppm. The defects recur (missing marking three times, burr, dimension, wrong material certificate), which suggests the 8Ds are not working. One 8D is overdue and qn:20004978 has no D8. Only EUR 150 per complaint is recharged, so the true cost to us is higher. part:310012 from this supplier has had 0 QNs.

Our volume outlook is growing and is shared with the supplier. part:310010 is forecast at 8150 pcs for the next 12 months against 7400 ordered in the last 12 (+10%). part:310012 is forecast at 2010 against 1786 (+12.5%), of which this supplier holds a 40% quota. Forecasts have been stable at 7250-8200 pcs for part:310010. This volume growth is a trade we can offer, for example a binding volume or a longer term in return for price and performance.

Some records support the supplier's case. Prices have fallen 7% since 2023 on both parts. On part:310012 its quality is clean, though it is 6.6% dearer than Wimbacher. The 9.5% increase it asks on part:310010 has no backing in its performance.

arguments.text: Part 310010 is sold below our full cost. Your own bottom-up should-cost is EUR 132.64 with no margin, and we deliver at 126.53. For four renewals in a row we accepted prices below full cost to keep the volume. Any foundry needs to earn its cost plus a margin to keep investing.

Our price for 310010 has fallen 7% since 2023 (136 to 126.53) while input costs rose. Labour in manufacturing is up 2.7% and is about a third of our cost. Basic iron and steel are up 6.5% in 12 months and 7.3% since January.

Your second source for 310010 is dearer and slower. Kalwisz quoted EUR 143.22 with 56 days' lead time, against our 42 days. Even with our requested increase we stay at or below the market alternative, and changing source costs you qualification time and the tooling move.
Partnership: in 2022 we kept supplying at the old price for a full quarter. We ask for fairness in return.
Your forecast for 310010 has grown to 8,150 pcs a year. We have the capacity and the willingness to secure that growth, but only at a price that covers cost.
Part 310012 has a perfect quality record (0 ppm) while Wimbacher had complaints. That justifies keeping our price level and our share.

weak_points: The 9.5% ask comes from a spreadsheet two years old, and I admitted we have not tracked costs since 2022. The checkable indices support only about +2-3%.
Power prices are -43% versus 2022 and -3.7% over 12 months. Our 'energy' argument is weak.
Notice was 51 days, but clause 3.1 requires 90 days before year end. A 1 November start breaches the contract.
On 310012 we are about 10% above our own should-cost (347.27 vs 383.06) and 24 EUR above Wimbacher at 359.17. A cut is exposed.
Delivery fell to class B amber, with 78.6% on time for 310010.
Quality on 310010 is weak: 12 supplier-caused complaints, about 777 ppm, and one 8D overdue.
We badly need cash: we asked for 10-day payment. Equity ratio is 24.7%.
In 2025 we quoted 142.5 for 310010 in the benchmark, which looks opportunistic.
wants: Payment in 10 days (or 14) in exchange for a cash discount of about 2%. This is the most valuable trade for us.
A binding annual volume for 310010 of about 8,000 pcs.
A 24-month contract term for planning security.
A higher quota on 310012 (from 40% towards 50%) if we lower that price.
An index clause on steel/iron for 310010 as an alternative to a large fixed increase.
Willingness to work through the quality issues together, and a cap on chargebacks.
red_lines: No further price cut on 310010. It must move up to at least about 131-132 (cost recovery).
On 310012, no cut below about 370 (our cost plus a minimal margin).
No higher ppm commitment or chargeback without a price that funds it.
No longer payment terms than 30 days.
red_team.opening: A warm, personal tone that recalls the 2022 partnership and the many years of supply. Keep the +9.5% (138.55) on 310010 as the headline, backed by the below-cost history and the dearer Polish quote. If the date is challenged, signal flexibility on timing (1 January). Hold 310012 unchanged at 383.06 and point to zero defects. Immediately offer a smaller increase in return for 10-day payment, binding volume and a 24-month term. Be ready to settle around +4-5% on 310010 from January, with only a small cut on 310012 in exchange for more quota.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that the smaller casing has been priced tightly for several years, and we do not want a key supplier to work at a loss. That is why we are prepared to discuss a fair adjustment on it. Our own estimate carries a real error band, so the gap is within that range rather than a proven loss. The fair basis is to adjust in line with the cost drivers that have actually moved, from the new calendar year as our agreement provides. The larger casing should be looked at in the same conversation, because there our estimate of your own plant leaves clear headroom.

We agree that labour and steel have risen, and we take both into account openly. Weighted by their share of the part's cost, together they explain a small single-digit adjustment, well short of the increase in your letter. Your letter also cites energy, yet the official index for industrial power is lower than a year ago, which reduces the total further. We are glad to share the official series we use, so that both sides work from the same figures.

We value your shorter lead time and your proximity, and we have no wish to move this part. That is exactly why we want a price that is fair to both sides and based on cost, not on what a dearer alternative would charge. The comparison to an outside quote does not change how much your costs have actually moved.

We remember that gesture and are grateful for it, and we want to answer it in kind. We propose to do so with things that help you directly: faster payment as you asked, a longer agreement with committed volumes, and a fair cost-based adjustment on the smaller casing from the new year. Partnership on our side also means bringing both casings into one balanced package.

We are pleased you can support the growth, and we see the higher volume as part of the solution. Higher volume spreads your fixed costs over more pieces, which should lessen the pressure on unit price rather than add to it. We are willing to make part of that growth binding over a longer term in exchange for a moderate adjustment.

Your quality on the larger casing has been excellent recently, and we appreciate it. Quality is expected at the agreed price, however, and does not by itself justify a price clearly above what the same part costs us from our other source. Our estimate of your own plant also shows room. If you can come closer to the market on this casing, we would gladly consider a larger share for you, together with the growing volume.

press: Under our framework agreement prices are fixed for each calendar year with the agreed notice, so we would apply any adjustment from the new year rather than from November.
The official power index is lower than a year ago, so we would ask you to look again at the energy part of your request.
We would be glad to send you the official labour, steel and power series we use, so that we both calculate from the same basis.
On the larger casing our estimate of your plant suggests there is room to come closer to the market, and we would welcome a proposal that lets us increase your share.
On-time delivery on the smaller casing has been below the contract target, and a firm commitment to improve it would make a longer agreement easier for us.
We have noted your wish for faster payment and are open to offering it as part of a balanced overall package.
